title: Data policies (DLP) for Copilot Studio agents
summary: The documented controls, commands, roles and enforcement behaviour are supported by Microsoft Learn. The page correctly qualifies classic data policies in ACP-only scopes and reports the conflicting connector-blocking and maker-guidance documentation rather than silently choosing one.

claims.claim: Connector blocking is reached in Power Platform admin center through Security > Data and privacy > Data policy > New Policy > Next > Add an environment > Next > Assign connectors > connector > three dots > Block.
claims.quote: Select Next. The Assign connectors page appears. ... Select the three dots (⋮) next to the connector, and then: ... To prevent agent makers from using the features associated with the connector, select Block.

claims.claim: Set-DlpPolicy -PolicyName <policy name> -UpdatedPolicy $UpdatedPolicy updates the policy using a policy update object.
claims.quote: Updates a policy by using the UpdatedPolicy DLPPolicyDefinition object. ... Set-DlpPolicy -PolicyName <String> -UpdatedPolicy <Object>

claims.claim: Endpoint configuration is reached through the stated data-policy wizard and connector three-dots menu, then Configure connector > Connector endpoints.
claims.quote: Select the three dots (⋮) next to the connector, and then: ... To allow or deny specific endpoints for SharePoint or public websites configured as knowledge sources, or for HTTP request: ... Select Configure connector > Connector endpoints.

claims.claim: New-PowerAppDlpPolicyConnectorConfigurations with TenantId, PolicyName and NewDlpPolicyConnectorConfigurations creates endpoint configurations.
claims.quote: New-PowerAppDlpPolicyConnectorConfigurations -TenantId $TenantId -PolicyName $PolicyName -NewDlpPolicyConnectorConfigurations $ConnectorConfigurations

claims.claim: The stated Maker guidance path selects environments or environment groups, Edit setting, and the Display guidance messaging in popovers for blocked items checkbox under Agent status.
claims.quote: In the panel, select the environments or environment groups you want to configure a custom guidance message for. Select Edit setting at the bottom of the panel to confirm your choice.

claims.claim: An API for Maker guidance is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Maker guidance" "API"; "Maker guidelines" PowerShell Dataverse API; Maker guidance Power Platform API rule based policies. Read both guidance pages, PowerShell support, Rule Based Policies and Create Rule Based Policy; no guidance rule inputs documented.

claims.claim: Tenant-level policies require Power Platform Administrator permissions.
claims.quote: To follow the steps described in this article for tenant-level policies, sign in as a user with the Power Platform Administrator role.

claims.claim: Environment-level policies require Environment Admin permissions for environments without Dataverse.
claims.quote: To follow the steps for environment-level policies, you need to have Power Apps Environment Admin permissions.

claims.claim: Environments with a Dataverse database require the System Administrator role instead.
claims.quote: For environments with a Dataverse database, you need to be assigned the System Administrator role instead.

claims.claim: PolicyName in the endpoint-configuration call takes the policy GUID.
claims.quote: In the following cmdlet, PolicyName refers to the unique GUID. Retrieve the data policy GUID by running the Get-DlpPolicy cmdlet.

claims.claim: Maker guidance is a preview feature.
claims.quote: Custom guidance message (preview)

claims.claim: Custom guidance can be configured per environment or environment group.
claims.quote: You can configure different messages for different environments and environment groups to tailor guidance by governance zone.

claims.claim: An environment group guidance message overrides an environment-level message.
claims.quote: The environment group message overrides the environment-level message.

claims.claim: Custom guidance messages support plain text only.
claims.quote: Custom guidance messages support plain text only and can be up to 400 characters.

claims.claim: Custom guidance messages have a 400-character limit.
claims.quote: Custom guidance messages support plain text only and can be up to 400 characters.

claims.claim: Data policies classify connectors and govern which connectors apps, flows and agents can use together.
claims.quote: The Business and Non-business data groups in data policies also continue to apply. ... If you rely on data groups to keep data from moving between specific connectors, keep the scope in mixed mode so that the data policy continues to apply.

claims.claim: Microsoft also calls these data loss prevention or DLP policies.
claims.quote: The policies that define how data can be shared are referred to as data loss prevention (DLP) policies.

claims.claim: The three connector data groups are Business, Non-Business and Blocked.
claims.quote: The three data groups are the Business data group, the Non-Business data group, and the Blocked data group.

claims.claim: Connectors in different data groups cannot share data.
claims.quote: You can't share data among connectors that are located in different groups.

claims.claim: An app or flow cannot combine SharePoint in Business with Gmail in Non-Business.
claims.quote: If you place SharePoint and Salesforce connectors in the Business group and you place Gmail in the Non-Business group, makers can't create an app or flow that uses both the SharePoint and Gmail connectors.

claims.claim: A Blocked connector cannot be used where the policy applies.
claims.quote: Blocked connectors can't be used where this policy is applied.

claims.claim: Data policy enforcement has been in effect for all tenants since early 2025.
claims.quote: Since early 2025, data policy enforcement is in effect for all tenants, as announced in the message center alert MC973179: Copilot Studio - Upcoming updates to data loss prevention enforcement.

claims.claim: Since March 2025 agents cannot be exempted from data policy enforcement.
claims.quote: Since March 2025, agents can't be exempted from data policy enforcement. It's no longer possible to exempt agents with a PowerShell command.

claims.claim: ACP-only mode ignores classic data policies for the affected scope.
claims.quote: ACP-only mode: ACP becomes the sole policy evaluator. Classic data policies are ignored but not deleted for the affected scope.

claims.claim: Classic data policies remain configured but unenforced in ACP-only mode.
claims.quote: Data policy configurations aren't deleted. They remain in place but aren't enforced while ACP-only mode is active.

claims.claim: Data policies must not be relied on for connector, endpoint or virtual-connector restrictions in ACP-only scopes.
claims.quote: Don't rely on a data policy for any control in an ACP-only scope, including custom connectors, HTTP connectors, endpoint filtering, and virtual connectors.

claims.claim: Virtual connectors are governance constructs not based on a REST API.
claims.quote: Virtual connectors are connectors that appear in data policies for administrators to control, but they're not based on a RESTful API.

claims.claim: Copilot Studio virtual connectors govern agent capabilities, including channels and triggers.
claims.quote: Use Copilot Studio connectors in the Power Platform admin center to configure data policies for the following common use cases: ... Block publishing to specific channels ... Block event triggers.

claims.where: What it is: connector table, authentication
claims.claim: Blocking Chat without Microsoft Entra ID authentication in Copilot Studio prevents unauthenticated agent publishing.
claims.quote: To prevent agent makers from publishing agents that don't require authentication, configure a data policy that blocks the connector Chat without Microsoft Entra ID authentication in Copilot Studio.

claims.where: What it is: connector table, HTTP
claims.claim: Blocking HTTP prevents publishing agents that make HTTP requests.
claims.quote: To prevent agent makers from publishing agents that make HTTP requests, configure a data policy that blocks the HTTP connector.

claims.where: What it is: connector table, Direct Line
claims.claim: Direct Line channels in Copilot Studio governs demo websites, custom websites and mobile-app channels.
claims.quote: Direct Line channels in Copilot Studio (applies to the Demo website, custom websites, mobile app, and other Direct Line channels)

claims.where: What it is: connector table, Teams and Microsoft 365
claims.claim: Microsoft Teams + Microsoft 365 Channel in Copilot Studio governs publishing to Microsoft 365 and Microsoft Teams.
claims.quote: Publishing to the Microsoft 365 and Microsoft Teams channel. | Microsoft Teams + Microsoft 365 Channel in Copilot Studio

claims.where: What it is: connector table, SharePoint
claims.claim: The matching SharePoint channel connector governs SharePoint publishing.
claims.quote: Publishing to the SharePoint channel. | SharePoint channel in Copilot Studio

claims.where: What it is: connector table, WhatsApp
claims.claim: The matching WhatsApp channel connector governs WhatsApp publishing.
claims.quote: Publishing to the WhatsApp channel. | WhatsApp channel in Copilot Studio

claims.where: What it is: connector table, Facebook
claims.claim: The matching Facebook channel connector governs Facebook publishing.
claims.quote: Publishing to the Facebook channel. | Facebook channel in Copilot Studio

claims.where: What it is: connector table, Dynamics 365 Customer Service
claims.claim: Omnichannel in Copilot Studio governs publishing to Dynamics 365 Customer Service.
claims.quote: Publishing to the Dynamics 365 Customer Service channel. | Omnichannel in Copilot Studio

claims.where: What it is: connector table, event triggers
claims.claim: The agent data policy page names Microsoft Copilot Studio as the connector to block for event triggers.
claims.quote: To prevent agent makers from adding event triggers to their agents or running automated evaluations by using an authenticated account, configure a data policy that blocks the Microsoft Copilot Studio connector.

claims.where: What it is: connector table, automated evaluations
claims.claim: Microsoft Copilot Studio is also the documented blocking connector for automated evaluations using authenticated accounts.
claims.quote: Using event triggers in Copilot Studio agents or running automated evaluations using authenticated accounts. | Microsoft Copilot Studio

claims.where: What it is: connector table, skills
claims.claim: Skills with Copilot Studio is the documented data policy connector for blocking Azure Bot Service skills.
claims.quote: To prevent agent makers from publishing agents that use Azure Bot Service skills, configure a data policy that blocks the Skills with Copilot Studio connector.

claims.where: What it is: connector table, Application Insights
claims.claim: Application Insights in Copilot Studio governs connecting agents to Application Insights.
claims.quote: Connecting agents with Application Insights. | Application Insights in Copilot Studio

claims.where: What it is: connector table, connector tools
claims.claim: Blocking the specific prebuilt or custom Power Platform connectors governs their use as agent tools.
claims.quote: To prevent agent makers from using Power Platform connectors as tools in Copilot Studio agents, configure a data policy with the connectors you want to block.

claims.where: What it is: Skills in Copilot Studio
claims.claim: Skills in Copilot Studio is a documented rule at environment and environment-group level.
claims.quote: Apply rules at the environment and environment group level to manage the use of skills in Copilot Studio.

claims.where: What it is: Skills in Copilot Studio
claims.claim: The Skills in Copilot Studio rule replaces the legacy skills virtual connectors.
claims.quote: This rule replaces the legacy Copilot Studio virtual connectors used in classic data policies to govern skills.

claims.where: summary; What it is; Governance controls
claims.claim: Blocking Power Platform connectors also blocks access to tools in connected MCP servers that rely on those connectors.
claims.quote: Blocking Power Platform connectors also blocks access to tools in connected MCP servers, which rely on Power Platform connectors for connectivity.

claims.where: What it is: How restrictions appear
claims.claim: Blocked connectors appear disabled in the maker experience.
claims.quote: A blocked connector appears disabled when a maker adds tools to an agent.

claims.where: What it is: How restrictions appear
claims.claim: Restricted channels appear disabled in the maker experience.
claims.quote: A restricted channel appears disabled when a maker attempts to add a channel while publishing an agent.

claims.where: What it is: How restrictions appear
claims.claim: Hovering over an unavailable capability explains the restriction.
claims.quote: Makers can hover over the unavailable capability to view information about why it's restricted.

claims.where: What it is: How restrictions appear
claims.claim: A draft agent that violates a data policy cannot be published.
claims.quote: When a data policy violation occurs, the Publish button becomes unavailable.

claims.where: What it is: How restrictions appear
claims.claim: Users interacting with a published agent in violation see DataLossPreventionViolation.
claims.quote: If your published agent is in violation of your data policies, users of the agent see a DataLossPreventionViolation error when trying to interact with it.

claims.where: What it is: How restrictions appear
claims.claim: The raw publishing-error JSON contains DlpViolationError.
claims.quote: $kind | DlpViolationError

claims.where: What it is: How restrictions appear
claims.claim: BlockedConnector is an example value of violationType in publishing-error JSON.
claims.quote: violationType | BlockedConnector

claims.where: What it is: How restrictions appear
claims.claim: For standard-harness agents, Agent status is on Overview, with Review showing blocking issues and warnings.
claims.quote: The Agent status summary appears on the overview page for an agent, under the Copilot details card. ... When you select Review in the Agent status summary, you see agent issues grouped by severity:

claims.where: What it is: How restrictions appear
claims.claim: The described Agent status experience is preview.
claims.quote: This article contains Microsoft Copilot Studio preview documentation and is subject to change.

claims.where: What it is; Why it matters
claims.claim: Data policies apply to Copilot Studio agents in environments within their scope, subject to the page's ACP-only qualification.
claims.quote: These data policies apply to Copilot Studio agents in the environments included in the policy's scope.

claims.claim: Add all environments makes a policy tenant-wide.
claims.quote: Add all environments: Adds all the environments in your entire tenant. This policy automatically applies to any new environment created in the tenant.

claims.claim: Tenant-level policies can include selected environments.
claims.quote: Tenant-level policies can be defined to include or exclude specific environments.

claims.claim: Tenant-level policies can exclude selected environments.
claims.quote: Tenant-level policies can be defined to include or exclude specific environments.

claims.claim: Learn says connectors introduced after 2019, including unauthenticated chat and Direct Line, are likely to be in the default Non-business group.
claims.quote: Connectors introduced after 2019, such as Chat without Microsoft Entra ID authentication in Copilot Studio or Direct Line channels in Copilot Studio, are likely to be part of the default "Non-business" group.

claims.claim: Learn says many organisations automatically block connectors in Non-business.
claims.quote: In many organizations, connectors in the "Non-business" group are automatically blocked.

claims.claim: Microsoft warns that policies blocking new connectors by default can cause production outages involving Direct Line or unauthenticated website agents.
claims.quote: Misaligned configurations, such as data policies blocking new connectors by default, could result in production outages. For example, essential features like Direct Line or unauthenticated agent deployments on websites might be unexpectedly blocked.

claims.claim: The data policy pages state no licence specific to the mechanism as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Platform data loss prevention data policies licensing price charge; "data policies" "license" "Power Platform". Read Data policies, Manage data policies, Connector classification, Configure data policies for agents and DLP policy creation; no separate data-policy licence stated.

claims.claim: The data policy pages publish no charge specific to the mechanism as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Platform data loss prevention data policies licensing price charge; "data policies" "license" "Power Platform". Read Data policies, Manage data policies, Connector classification, Configure data policies for agents and DLP policy creation; no separate data-policy charge stated.

claims.claim: Connector usage can have its own licensing requirements.
claims.quote: Some connectors require specific licensing, and if your license doesn't include them, you can't see them.

claims.claim: The Class column on Assign connectors identifies whether connector usage needs a Premium licence.
claims.quote: Class | Indicates whether connector usage requires a Premium license or is it included in the Built-in/Standard license for Power Platform.

claims.claim: Learn says connectors not included in the viewer's licence are not visible to that viewer.
claims.quote: Some connectors require specific licensing, and if your license doesn't include them, you can't see them.

claims.claim: New connectors normally enter the policy's designated default data group.
claims.quote: You must designate one data group as the default group to automatically classify any new connectors added to Microsoft Power Platform after you create your policy.

claims.claim: The initial default group is Non-Business.
claims.quote: Initially, the Non-Business group is the default group for new connectors and all services.

claims.claim: New nonblockable connectors enter Non-Business even when the default is Blocked.
claims.quote: If Microsoft adds any new connectors that can't be blocked and you set the default group for the data policy as Blocked, these connectors are automatically marked as Non-Business instead of Blocked.

claims.claim: A Blocked default group places new blockable connectors in Blocked.
claims.quote: If the new connector setting is Blocked, any new connectors that are blockable are mapped to Blocked, as expected.

claims.claim: Published agents in violation show errors requiring a policy or agent-configuration correction.
claims.quote: Agent users should contact their admin to resolve the issue. The admin can check the data policy violations and update the policies or the agent configuration as needed.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Enforcement takes time
claims.claim: Full data policy enforcement can take 24 hours in the most extreme cases.
claims.quote: For the most extreme cases, the latency for full enforcement is 24 hours.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Enforcement takes time
claims.claim: Full data policy enforcement occurs within an hour in most cases.
claims.quote: In most cases, it's within an hour.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Enforcement takes time
claims.claim: Resources found in violation are suspended or quarantined.
claims.quote: If a violation occurs, put the app, flow, or chatbot in to a suspended or quarantine state so that it can't operate.

claims.where: Risks and limits: No channel left; What to check
claims.claim: Agents cannot be published without an allowed, configured channel.
claims.quote: If makers don't configure their agents for a channel that isn't blocked (Direct Line channels are allowed by default), or if the administrators don't allow any channel, agents can't be published.

claims.where: Risks and limits: No channel left; What to check
claims.claim: Direct Line channels are allowed by default.
claims.quote: Direct Line channels are allowed by default

claims.where: Risks and limits: Some connectors cannot be blocked
claims.claim: Data policies cannot block some connectors that drive core Power Platform functionality.
claims.quote: To ensure core user scenarios remain fully functional, you can't block connectors that drive core Microsoft Power Platform functionality, such as Dataverse, Approvals, and Notifications.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Some connectors cannot be blocked; Open questions
claims.claim: The connector classification page includes Microsoft Copilot Studio in its nonblockable list.
claims.quote: The following connectors can't be blocked by using data policies. ... Microsoft Copilot Studio

claims.where: Risks and limits: Some connectors cannot be blocked; What to check
claims.claim: The Blockable column indicates whether a connector can be blocked.
claims.quote: Blockable | Indicates if the connectors can be blocked or not.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risks and limits; Governance controls
claims.claim: Connector endpoint filtering is preview.
claims.quote: This is a preview feature.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risks and limits; What to check
claims.claim: The described agent endpoint filtering evaluates static design-time endpoints rather than environment variables, custom inputs or runtime-bound endpoints.
claims.quote: Endpoint filtering rules don't apply to environment variables, custom inputs, or any endpoint dynamically created at runtime. Only static endpoints are evaluated in the app, flow, or chatbot designers.

claims.claim: A dynamic endpoint can bypass the described filtering rule.
claims.quote: A maker builds a cloud flow that defines the SQL Server and database inside variables, and then uses those variables as input to the connection definition. As a result, the endpoint filtering rules aren't evaluated, and the cloud flow executes successfully.

claims.claim: For SharePoint knowledge, Purview DLP scoped to Microsoft 365 Copilot can restrict Copilot Studio agents for Teams, SharePoint and Microsoft 365 Copilot based on a sensitivity label.
claims.quote: When the knowledge source is SharePoint, a DLP policy scoped to the Microsoft 365 Copilot location can restrict agents built in Copilot Studio for Microsoft Teams, SharePoint, and Microsoft 365 Copilot from processing sensitive content based on a specified sensitivity label.

claims.claim: Copilot Studio virtual connectors are evolving into dedicated governance rules separate from data policies and ACP.
claims.quote: Copilot Studio virtual connectors are evolving into their own dedicated governance rules, separate from both data policies and ACP.

claims.claim: Policies are created and changed in Power Platform admin center.
claims.quote: Administrators can configure Copilot Studio and Power Platform data policies in the Power Platform admin center.

claims.claim: The Copilot Studio guide places Add an environment before Assign connectors.
claims.quote: 5. Select Next. The Add an environment page appears. ... 6. Select Next. The Assign connectors page appears.

claims.claim: Endpoint filtering configures allowed or denied endpoints for specific supported connectors, including HTTP, within a data policy.
claims.quote: It's configured within a data policy, and it's exclusively available for the following connectors: ... HTTP ... This opens a side panel where you specify an ordered list of Allow or Deny URL patterns.

claims.claim: Tenant-level policies classify custom connectors by Host URL pattern, separately from endpoint filtering.
claims.quote: You can classify custom connectors by name in environment-level data policies and by host URL pattern in tenant-level data policies.

claims.claim: Environment admins classify custom connectors on the Connectors page of Data Policies.
claims.quote: Environment admins can now find all the custom connectors in their environments alongside prebuilt connectors on the Connectors page in Data Policies. Similar to prebuilt connectors, you can classify custom connectors into Blocked, Business, or Non-Business categories.

claims.claim: Set-PowerAppDlpErrorSettings updates the data policy error contact email and Learn more link.
claims.quote: Use the Set-PowerAppDlpErrorSettings PowerShell cmdlet to add an email address and a "Learn more" link to the data policy error messages. ... These settings apply to all Power Platform apps within the specified tenant.

claims.claim: Managed Environments sharing limits govern sharing of agents that require authentication.
claims.quote: You configure the sharing limits for agents as a Managed Environments control in the Power Platform admin center. ... Sharing limits only apply to agents that require authentication.

claims.claim: Microsoft's ACP migration guidance asks administrators to match dedicated channel, authentication and skills settings to their current virtual-connector restrictions.
claims.quote: Configure the dedicated agent settings for the same scope so that they match your current Copilot Studio virtual connector settings: ... Agent access channels ... Authentication for agents ... Skills in Copilot Studio

claims.claim: The separate preview admin guide calls its control Maker guidelines.
claims.quote: Configure maker guidelines for Copilot Studio (preview)

claims.claim: The Maker guidelines guide places the guidance in the Copilot Studio Review pane.
claims.quote: The guidance appears in the Copilot Studio Review pane.

claims.claim: The Maker guidelines guide says the control is available only for managed environments.
claims.quote: Maker guidelines is available only for managed environments.

claims.claim: The Maker guidelines guide uses Edit rule for environment groups in the Copilot area.
claims.quote: Environment group in the Copilot area: Select Copilot > Settings, and then select Maker guidelines. Select the Environment groups tab, select the environment group, and then select Edit rule.

claims.claim: The data policy error email and Learn more settings apply to all Power Platform apps in the specified tenant.
claims.quote: These settings apply to all Power Platform apps within the specified tenant.

claims.where: controls[2].governs; Governance controls; What to check
claims.claim: The environment-level custom guidance message is shown when makers encounter blocked or disabled capabilities.
claims.quote: As an admin, you can set an environment-level guidance message for users when they encounter a blocked or disabled capability. This plain-text message replaces the default Contact your admin prompt.

claims.claim: Policy update automation can change connector data-group classification.
claims.quote: This sample calls data policy APIs in Microsoft.PowerApps.Administration.PowerShell to create, read, update and remove data policies. ... Update policy to move connector across groups (Business, Non-business, and Blocked).
